title: Seated Row Machine (Selectorized)
summary: A selectorized seated row with a chest pad and fixed handles, which keeps the torso still so the mid-back and lats do the work.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: commercial gym machine (this exercise's own machine).

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for upper back (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly upper back total.
Library rating 0.75 for lats (main mover): each working set adds 0.75 of a set to the weekly lats total.
Library rating 0.55 for traps (helper): each working set adds 0.55 of a set to the weekly traps total.
Library rating 0.45 for rear delts (helper): each working set adds 0.45 of a set to the weekly rear delts total.
Library rating 0.45 for biceps (helper): each working set adds 0.45 of a set to the weekly biceps total.

setup.text: Set the seat so the handles are at about lower-chest height, with your chest on the pad.
Row the handles back until your elbows pass your torso.
Let them go forward until your arms are straight and your shoulder blades spread.

form_cues.cue: Keep the chest on the pad
Keep your chest on the pad. Don't lean back to finish the rep.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train pain-free.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: More stretch emphasis, Less upper-back focus.

alternatives.goal_label: Home gym: no equipment / bar only
alternatives.why: Swap sheet: Less stable, Lower loading potential, More technical.
